The Integration Pitch

One record, one global network

The Ehlers-Danlos Society runs on a patchwork of systems that each solve one problem well: the DICE Global Registry and biobank capture genetic and patient-reported data, the CORE Network routes patients into dozens of independently-run Centers of Excellence, and EDS ECHO case-mentors thousands of clinicians across 58 countries. As Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Dacre Knight sits at the center of all three — and, since September 2025, at the bedside too, having left his post founding Mayo Clinic's EDS Clinic to launch UVA Health's new $3M EDS & Hypermobility Disorders Center, one of only about 15 dedicated EDS treatment programs in the country.

The highest-leverage moment is now: a brand-new clinical program is standing up its own record at the exact moment the Society is scaling the registry, the CORE Network, and ECHO past the point manual data-sharing can keep up. Every referral into a CORE center, every registry entry, every ECHO case consult currently depends on clinicians re-entering the same multisystem patient history by hand — the opposite of the coordinated, low-burden care EDS and HSD patients need.

Vorro gives the Society and its network a single interoperability layer — FHIR, HL7, and C-CDA pipes that let UVA's new center, Mayo's clinic, and any future CORE site exchange records with the DICE Registry and each other without custom point-to-point work, plus ambient documentation built for the long, multisystem visits EDS and HSD care requires. For an organization built on connecting 58 countries of clinicians and patients, that connective tissue should run through the data, too.
